components.name: Install Pill

components.name: Download Pill

components.css: .ds-download { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 14px; background: transparent; color: oklch(0.94 0.015 80); border: 1px solid oklch(0.74 0.18 55 / 0.60); border-radius: 9999px; font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), background-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-download:hover { border-color: oklch(0.74 0.18 55); background-color: oklch(0.74 0.18 55 / 0.10); }

components.css: .ds-alpha { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: oklch(0.52 0.010 80); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-alpha__dot { width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 9999px; background: oklch(0.74 0.18 55 / 0.80); }

components.name: Play Button (Hero)

components.name: FAQ Row
components.description: Native details/summary. Plain row, hairline divider above and below, halation-orange '+' that rotates to 'x' on open.
components.html:
Does my footage leave my machine?+

No. Everything happens locally on your GPU. There is no telemetry and no upload.
components.css: .ds-faq { padding: 24px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid oklch(0.22 0.014 220 / 0.80); transition: background-color 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); border-radius: 2px; } .ds-faq:hover { background-color: oklch(0.17 0.013 220 / 0.30); } .ds-faq summary { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px; cursor: pointer; list-style: none; } .ds-faq summary::-webkit-details-marker { display: none; } .ds-faq__q { font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 24px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.015em; color: oklch(0.94 0.015 80); padding-right: 16px; } .ds-faq__plus { color: oklch(0.74 0.18 55); font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 13px; transition: transform 300ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-faq[open] .ds-faq__plus { transform: rotate(45deg); } .ds-faq__a { margin: 16px 0 0; max-width: 68ch; color: oklch(0.72 0.012 80); font-family: 'Inter Tight', Inter, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.55; }

narrative.overview:
Hance is a film-look engine that runs on your machine, in your terminal, on your GPU. The site is its proof: the page itself looks color-graded. A drenched, warm-cyan-tinted near-black surface holds the entire experience like an unlit darkroom; a single halation-orange accent does all the signaling. There is no chrome theatre here. Type carries the page. The product gets out of its own way.

The system rejects every visual reflex of its category. It is not the navy-and-cyan dev-tool dashboard. It is not the cream-and-charcoal SaaS landing page. It is not the neon-on-black AI-tool aesthetic. It is not the Adobe-blue creative-cloud marketing site. It refuses gradient text, glassmorphic stat tiles, identical icon-card grids, and isometric illustration. Every section breathes differently; nothing is wrapped in a default container 'for safety'.
keyCharacteristics: Drenched warm-cyan-black surface, one halation-orange accent (≤8% of any viewport).
Type-led hierarchy: oversized grotesk display, mono captions, no decorative icon families.
Variable vertical rhythm. Each section sets its own pace.
Single-page, single-job: every block bends toward download.
The placeholder itself is graded. There is no 'neutral' surface anywhere in the system.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: Halation Orange is used on no more than 8% of any rendered viewport. It is the safelight. If the page starts feeling orange, an accent is misplaced.

rules.name: The Tinted-Black Rule
rules.body: Pure #000 and pure #fff are forbidden. Every neutral carries chroma 0.010–0.015 toward cyan (surfaces) or warm yellow (type).

rules.name: The No Second Accent Rule
rules.body: No green-success, no red-error, no link-blue. Either Halation Orange handles it, or type weight handles it.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Sans for content, mono for the machine. Never set running prose in mono and never set a CLI snippet in sans.

rules.name: The Tight-Stack Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type are set with tight leading (0.92 / 0.95) and aggressive negative tracking (-0.045em / -0.025em).

rules.name: The One Paragraph Rule
rules.body: The hero subhead is the only Body Large in the system. Every other paragraph is Body.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows on cards, panels, popovers, or buttons. Raise tonal value, not shadow.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders and dividers are exactly 1px in Cinema Black Edge. Halation-orange borders are reserved for interactive affordances.

rules.name: The Halation-Once Rule
rules.body: The orange glow shadow appears on one element per page (the play button). If a second needs it, the first one stops having it.

dos: Do keep Halation Orange usage at or below 8% of any viewport.
Do tint every neutral. Surfaces toward cyan; type toward warm.
Do set display and headline type at tight leading and aggressive negative tracking.
Do vary vertical rhythm between sections.
Do carry CLI snippets in JetBrains Mono and prose in Inter Tight.
Do pair every accent surface with the alpha-status copy nearby.
Do prefer hairlines, tonal layering, and whitespace over panels and shadows.
donts: Don't use #000 or #fff anywhere in the system.
Don't introduce a second accent color.
Don't set gradient text via background-clip: text.
Don't use glassmorphism decoratively. The hero play button is the only blur.
Don't wrap sections in cards or three-column feature-card grids.
Don't add isometric illustrations, mesh backgrounds, Trusted-by logo strips, stock-photo lifestyle shots, neon-cyan grids, or AI-mesh gradients.
Don't use side-stripe borders greater than 1px.
Don't write em dashes in copy.
Don't animate layout properties; animate transform, opacity, filter, clip-path. Always ease-out-expo or ease-out-quart.
Don't reuse the Halation Glow on more than one element per page.
